name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen123
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - MOMENTUM DOES NOT PERSIST:
- change_1m_bps beyond ±5 almost always pauses or reverses in the next minute, rarely extends
- change_1m_bps beyond ±8 strongly signals exhaustion; expect mean reversion of roughly 50-70% of the move
- After change_1m_bps of +9 to +12, expect delta around -5 to -7 bps
- After change_1m_bps of -9 to -12, expect delta around +5 to +7 bps
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±12, expect even larger reversion: delta magnitude 60-80% of the original move, opposite sign
- When change_1m_bps is +3 to +6, expect delta around -2 to -3 bps
- When change_1m_bps is -3 to -6, expect delta around +2 to +3 bps
- Consecutive moves in one direction for 2+ minutes make a third minute of continuation very unlikely
- change_5m_bps beyond ±25 adds to exhaustion: widen spread and increase reversion magnitude

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.70 is aggressive buying; below 0.30 is aggressive selling
- Flow in the *last completed minute* often exhausts: extreme values (>0.75 or <0.25) frequently reverse as the aggressor finishes
- When last minute shows taker_buy_share <0.20 (heavy selling), add +1 to +2 bps to predicted delta
- When last minute shows taker_buy_share >0.80 (heavy buying), subtract 1 to 2 bps from predicted delta
- Moderate taker_buy_share (0.40-0.60) after recent volatility does NOT signal continuation - still expect reversion

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

CRITICAL RULES FOR HALF_WIDTH_BPS - THE DOMINANT SOURCE OF LOSSES:

After large moves, you MUST widen significantly:
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±8: half_width at least 5 bps (not 4, not 3 - minimum 5)
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±10: half_width at least 6 bps
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±12: half_width at least 7 bps
- After change_5m_bps beyond ±20: add +1 bps to minimum half_width
- After change_5m_bps beyond ±50: half_width at least 7 bps regardless of change_1m

The pattern in losses: half_width of 2 bps after change_1m of ±9 to ±12 gets run over repeatedly.
Example 6 shows the error: change_1m_bps was +9.6, harness used half_width 2.0, got run over (realized -9.6 when predicting -5.7±2).
Example 8 shows the error: change_1m_bps was +9.25, harness used half_width 2.0, got run over (realized -2.7 when predicting -5.7±2).

After smaller moves:
- After change_1m_bps of ±3 to ±5: half_width at least 4 bps
- After change_1m_bps of ±5 to ±8: half_width at least 4.5 bps
- When last minute taker_buy_share was extreme (>0.75 or <0.25): half_width at least 3.5 bps

Default for quiet conditions (change_1m within ±2, change_5m within ±5, taker_buy_share 0.4-0.6): 2.5-3 bps

Never use half_width under 2 bps.

The fundamental rule: widen when price just moved sharply. Getting run over (price outside your quote) scores negative and loses money. A wide quote that doesn't trade scores zero - which is vastly better than getting run over. Example 4 succeeded with half_width 3.7 after change_1m of +1.5 and change_5m of -4.8.

Skill comes from:
1. Staying silent (delta near zero, width 2.5-3 bps) when nothing will happen - most minutes
2. Predicting mean reversion after big moves with the CORRECT magnitude
3. WIDENING SPREAD APPROPRIATELY when volatility just occurred - this is not optional

Decision template based on change_1m_bps:
- If change_1m_bps > +12: predict delta -7 to -10 bps, half_width at least 7 bps
- If change_1m_bps +10 to +12: predict delta -6 to -8 bps, half_width at least 6 bps
- If change_1m_bps +8 to +10: predict delta -5 to -7 bps, half_width at least 5 bps
- If change_1m_bps +5 to +8: predict delta -3 to -5 bps, half_width at least 4.5 bps
- If change_1m_bps +3 to +5: predict delta -2 to -3 bps, half_width at least 4 bps
- If change_1m_bps -3 to -5: predict delta +2 to +3 bps, half_width at least 4 bps
- If change_1m_bps -5 to -8: predict delta +3 to +5 bps, half_width at least 4.5 bps
- If change_1m_bps -8 to -10: predict delta +5 to +7 bps, half_width at least 5 bps
- If change_1m_bps -10 to -12: predict delta +6 to +8 bps, half_width at least 6 bps
- If change_1m_bps < -12: predict delta +7 to +10 bps, half_width at least 7 bps
- If change_1m within ±2 AND change_5m within ±5: predict delta near 0, half_width 2.5-3 bps

Adjust delta for extreme tape (but do not reduce half_width):
- If taker_buy_share <0.20 in last minute: add +1 to +2 bps to predicted delta
- If taker_buy_share >0.80 in last minute: subtract 1 to 2 bps from predicted delta

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast (half_width well under 10 bps and strong directional conviction) justifies acting. When uncertain, widen half_width rather than guess.

The scoring system rewards calling direction correctly on moves that actually happen, and penalizes being wrong. Standing aside (wide quote) scores zero. Getting run over (realized price outside your quote) scores negative and loses money. 

The pattern of past errors: repeatedly using half_width of 2 bps after change_1m_bps of ±9 to ±12. This must stop. The minimum after such moves is 5-6 bps, not 2. Example 5 shows partial success: change_1m was +54 bps (massive), used half_width 7.4, still got run over but at least recognized the volatility. Example 6 and 8 show the failure mode: change_1m around +9.5, used half_width 2.0, got run over immediately.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. Most minutes stay within 2 bps of unchanged. Only call large moves with strong evidence.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
